analysis: Only scripts/test-provider-release-toolchain.py changed (head lines 1-285): a unit-test file for the CI release toolchain selection (prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh) and CMake install (install-release-cmake.sh). It adds helper read_github_env, tests for SDK 27.0/27.2 qualification acceptance, release mode accepting only SDK 27.2 with Swift 6.4.2, unknown-mode refusal, fail-closed on wrong SDK, Xcode selection preference and explicit DEVELOPER_DIR handling, and CMake tool-cache use versus download. Tests use temp directories and stubbed uname/curl/xcrun, so they do not install software or touch the network. No runtime provider code, protocol, key custody, attestation, or cache code is changed, so the T-041 cache threat and the TB-002/TB-003/TB-011 boundaries are unaffected. The tests assert fail-closed behavior (no GITHUB_ENV written on refusal), which supports the supply-chain posture rather than weakening it. Unverified contract: the actual shell scripts (prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh, install-release-cmake.sh) were not supplied, so whether they implement the behavior these tests assert, including the release-mode SDK 27.2 and Swift 6.4.2 pin, and any CMake checksum verification on download, is outside the evidence. The scripts' diff, if changed in this PR, should be reviewed in another unit. No security regression is identified in this file.
